title: Polymers
examples: What is the difference between addition and condensation polymerization?
How do I draw the repeat unit for a polymer?
Can you give an example of a polymer made by condensation?

explain.say: Today we are learning about polymers, which are very long chains of repeating units.
First we look at addition polymerization, where monomers join without losing any atoms.
For example, ethene monomers can join together to form polyethylene, a common plastic.
Next is condensation polymerization, which involves the joining of monomers with the loss of a small molecule.
A common example is the formation of nylon, which involves the loss of water when amino acids join.
In everyday life, think about making plastic bags; this often uses addition polymerization.

faq.q: What is the difference between addition and condensation polymerization?
faq.a: In addition polymerization, monomers simply join together without losing any atoms. In condensation polymerization, a small molecule like water is lost when the monomers join.
asks: Does water get lost in condensation?
What happens when monomers join in addition?

faq.q: Do I need to know the chemical formula for every polymer?
faq.a: No, you mainly need to know the general process. Understanding the loss of a small molecule is key for condensation.
asks: Is the repeat unit the same as the monomer?
What is the general rule for condensation?

faq.a: The repeat unit is the segment of the monomer that keeps repeating along the entire length of the polymer chain.
asks: How do I draw the repeating part?
Is the repeat unit the whole polymer?

faq.q: Can polymers be made using both methods?
faq.a: Yes, many different plastics and materials are formed using either addition or condensation reactions.
asks: Are there examples of both types?
Which method is used for nylon?

faq.q: What is the simplest type of polymer?
faq.a: The simplest are often made from simple alkenes through addition polymerization.
asks: What is the basic building block?
Can you name a simple addition polymer?

facts: Polymers are large molecules made of many smaller units called monomers.
Addition polymerization involves the joining of monomers with no atoms lost.
Condensation polymerization occurs when a small molecule, like water, is eliminated.
The structure repeats along the entire length of the polymer chain.
